title: Sell Mineral Rights in Norvelt, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Norvelt, PA
metaDescription: Norvelt, Westmoreland County mineral rights owner? We buy oil and gas interests tied to the old New Deal homestead tracts, cash offers, no obligation.
heroLead: Norvelt was built as a New Deal homestead community back in the 1930s, and a good number of the small acreage lots laid out then still carry the original mineral rights split among the descendants of the families who first settled there.
intro: There's a particular kind of ownership history in Norvelt that we don't see everywhere — homestead lots of a few acres each, subdivided by federal planners rather than a private landowner, which means the mineral interests under those lots were often severed or leased in patterns that don't match the surrounding farmland. If you inherited one of those parcels and have no idea what your fraction is worth, that confusion is normal, not a sign you're missing something obvious.

sections.heading: The Homestead-Lot Ownership Puzzle
paragraphs: Because Norvelt's original lots were small and uniform, mineral interests here tend to be modest fractional shares rather than large tracts, and many were leased as part of a bigger unit that also picked up neighboring farmland outside the homestead boundary. That means your royalty, if you have one, may be tied to a well pad you've never seen and don't need to see to get paid.

Westmoreland County is squarely in the wet-gas window, which historically has drawn more sustained operator interest than the dry-gas counties to the northeast, so units around Norvelt have generally seen more consistent activity than some rural stretches of the state.

sections.heading: Clearing Up Old Family Paperwork
paragraphs: A fair number of Norvelt homestead deeds passed through multiple generations without a formal estate settlement, especially on lots that stopped being actively farmed decades ago. We pull the recorded chain of title from the Westmoreland County recorder of deeds in Greensburg and tell you plainly what, if anything, needs to be cleared up before a sale can close — often it's simpler than families expect.

faqs.question: My homestead lot is only a couple acres. Is it too small to sell?
faqs.answer: No. We buy small fractional interests regularly in this area; size alone doesn't disqualify a tract, though it does factor into the offer.

faqs.question: Nobody in my family knows if the minerals were ever leased. How do we find out?
faqs.answer: We check the county lease records for you as part of our review, at no cost, before you have to decide anything.

faqs.question: Will selling affect who owns the surface lot?
faqs.answer: No, mineral and surface ownership are separate. Selling your mineral interest has no effect on the homestead lot itself if your family still holds the surface.
